Taking Notes Like a Researcher: 1. So they understand the idea, do not copy someone else's words, and can explain it themselves. 2. Example: "weighs about a penny (Tiny Flyers)". 3. Example: "flapping uses lots of energy, so needs nectar from hundreds of flowers daily (Tiny Flyers)". 4. It names the source, so the researcher can find the fact again and give credit. 5. Example: How far do hummingbirds migrate? What do hummingbirds do at night?
Sea Otter Research Notes: 1. thickest fur of any animal, up to about a million hairs per stamp-sized patch; air trapped in fur keeps water off skin; no blubber; groom for hours (Kelp); dirty fur makes them dangerously cold (Care Center). 2. eat about one quarter of body weight daily; crabs, clams, snails, sea urchins; crack shells on a rock on their chest (Kelp); fed clams and squid at the center (Care Center). 3. pups depend on mothers about six months; carried on mother's chest; mother grooms the fur; pup floats like a cork; wrapped in kelp while mother hunts (Care Center). 4. otters eat urchins; fewer urchins chew through kelp; kelp forests stay healthy for fish and other animals; keystone species (Kelp). 5. Example: how mothers raise pups, or how caretakers prepare a pup to return to the wild. 6. Example headings: Staying Warm, Finding Food, Raising Pups, Protecting the Kelp Forest.
Report: All About Sea Otters: No single answer. An Advanced report introduces sea otters, has two or more sections with headings, uses facts from both texts (one from each at least), defines at least two topic words, uses linking words, ends with a conclusion and names both sources.
Scoring tip: copying long sentences from a text is Developing on the notes criterion even when the facts are correct; for the report, check development against both sources, not only the first.
title: Answer key: Researching and Reporting
